reason: The operative contract (problem.txt) requires abs(actual - cbrt(x)) <= 1e-6*abs(cbrt(x)) for every finite FP16 value, with zeros mapping to zero. Decisive evidence is the exhaustive runtime sweep of all 63,488 finite FP16 bit patterns (both signs, all exponents and mantissas) through the actual kernel on the frozen T4/PyTorch 2.8/Triton 3.4 environment: max relative error 6.32e-7 < 1e-6 with 0 violations (probe t9). This single exhaustive test subsumes the entire legal domain, so no distribution-dependent blind spot remains. It also directly rebuts c1 (accuracy budget, worst case at input 10008.0, margin ~37%), and c3 (all 2,046 signed subnormals run separately, max error 5.61e-7, 0 violations, confirming the quotient/scale bit splice handles subnormal-derived FP32 exponents correctly). c2 was rebutted by the exact FP32 pipeline emulation (t10): truncated 4-decimal coefficients yield post-Newton error 5.96e-7, within tolerance, while a least-squares best-fit quadratic would actually be worse — so truncation causes no violation. Zero handling is contract-legal (magnitude==0 restores x; either sign accepted per problem.txt). All claims are in-scope with scope evidence citing the problem.txt domain, all are rebutted, no open claims remain, and the Skeptic signed off with no new claims after reviewing the latest evidence. Verdict: trust.
